**BlueCall 1.2**: call over direct Wi-Fi as well as Bluetooth, and Bluetooth earphones that join a call the moment they connect.

> **Pre-release.** This build compiles and passes its unit tests, but it hasn't been tested on real phones yet. Please report what works and what doesn't.

### What's new
- **Wi-Fi calling:** phone-to-phone Wi-Fi (Wi-Fi Aware). No router, network or internet needed.
  - Each nearby phone shows a **Bluetooth** button, a **Wi-Fi** button, or both. Pick one for each call.
  - The call screen and the notification show which one the call uses.
  - Wi-Fi calls use higher-quality audio (Opus at 32 kbps) and usually reach a little further.
  - With Bluetooth off, BlueCall stays online over Wi-Fi.
- **Earphones, car kits and watches:** calls are now registered with Android's own calling system.
  - Bluetooth earphones that connect **during a call** take it over, even from the speaker or earpiece.
  - When they disconnect, the call goes back to where it was: speaker stays speaker.
  - Earphone, car and watch buttons answer and hang up.
  - With several devices connected, the call screen lists each one by name.
  - A SIM call puts the BlueCall call on hold, with a **Resume** button afterwards.
  - On phones without Android's calling system, BlueCall switches devices the same way itself.
- **Settings › Calls:** new "Wi-Fi calling" and "Use system calling" switches, both on by default.

### Requirements and limits
- **Wi-Fi Aware on both phones:** Wi-Fi calls need it. Many Galaxy S, Note and Fold models have it; most A-series phones don't. Phones without it show only the Bluetooth button.
- **Android 12:** Wi-Fi calls also need location access with Location turned on. That's Android's rule for Wi-Fi Aware there. BlueCall asks only if you want Wi-Fi calls, and never uses your location.
- **Deep sleep or hotspot:** Android pauses Wi-Fi Aware while a phone is in deep sleep or running a hotspot. Wi-Fi calls reach it again once it wakes; Bluetooth calls always get through.
- **No encryption:** calls are not end-to-end encrypted, over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth.

### New permissions
- **Nearby Wi-Fi devices:** part of the "Nearby devices" prompt on Android 13+. Used to find and connect to phones over Wi-Fi.
- **Network access:** Android requires it for any phone-to-phone connection. The Wi-Fi link has no internet, and BlueCall never connects to the internet.
- **Calling app:** to register calls with Android's calling system.
- **Location** (Android 12 only): see above.

### Battery
- With Wi-Fi calling on, BlueCall uses a little more battery while online. The Wi-Fi chip answers other phones on its own in short scheduled windows, with no app wake-ups.
- Turn it off in Settings › Calls if you only use Bluetooth.
- After **Exit**, nothing of BlueCall runs at all, as before.

### Install
Download `BlueCall-v1.2.0.apk` on **both** phones and open it.
- **Updating:** it installs **over v1.1.0** and keeps your settings, because both are signed with the same test key.
- **Fresh install:** allow *Install unknown apps* when asked, then grant **Nearby devices**, **Microphone** and **Notifications**.

Requirements: Android 12 or newer with Bluetooth LE.

### Signing
Signed with BlueCall's **public test key** (`app/signing/bluecall-test.jks`). Check the download against `SHA256SUMS.txt`:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt
```

### Testing
See the [two-phone test checklist](https://github.com/codemew/BlueCall/blob/v1.2.0/README.md#testing-on-two-phones). It covers Wi-Fi calls, earphones joining mid-call, and a SIM call during a BlueCall call.
